title: Retail Installment Contracts: Reversal of Returned Payments
content:
**Once only.** On Retail Installment Contracts, a posted payment can be returned only once; the contract's money history is checked for an existing return linked to that payment.

**What a return reverses.** The return reverses exactly the interest, principal and fee portions the original payment applied, restores any installment credit it gave (moving the next due date back where needed), restores the unpaid interest carried to its value before the returned payment posted, and re-establishes any fee portion as a reversed fee payment linked to the return.

**Fee on a return.** The clause "A return whose return reason is in the fee-bearing return reasons carries the returned-payment fee as a returned-payment fee linked to the return row and dated on the return date, unless the monthly cap of returned-payment fees are already assessed and unwaived on the contract in that calendar month, in which case no fee is assessed" is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis for the returned-payment fee.

**Returns that carry no fee.** A return for an unauthorized debit or a bank error carries no returned-payment fee, and a returned-payment fee is never charged on a payment that was itself a fee settlement only.

**Late charges after a return.** A late charge that becomes due because the return reopened an installment is assessed under the late-charge rules on its own date; the return itself never backdates a late charge.

**Certified-funds count.** Fee-bearing returns count toward the certified-funds-only threshold of the payment channel rules.

| Portion of the original payment | Effect of the return |
|---|---|
| interest portion | reversed; unpaid interest carried restored to its value before the payment posted |
| principal portion | restored to the principal balance |
| fee portion | re-established as a reversed fee payment linked to the return |
| installment credit given | restored; next due date moved back where needed |

**Hypothetical case.** A 410.00 payment applied 120.00 to interest, 265.00 to principal and 25.00 to fees, and advanced the next due date from 1 May to 1 June. Its return restores 265.00 of principal, records a 25.00 reversed fee payment, restores the unpaid interest carried to its earlier value, and moves the next due date back to 1 May.

superseded_clauses: A return whose return_reason is in fee_bearing_return_reasons carries returned_payment_fee_usd as a returned_payment_fee linked to the return row and dated on the return date, unless returned_payment_fee_monthly_cap returned-payment fees are already assessed and unwaived on the contract in that calendar month (contract_msr_returned_fees_in_month), in which case no fee is assessed.
